metadata.title: Tribal Mental Health Patients chained in Temple | मानसिक बीमारी से आदिवासी अछूते नहीं हैं
metadata.description:
The temple in Chitrakot, Chhattisgarh, presents a disturbing scene where individuals with mental health conditions are chained and subjected to inhumane treatment. Some of these patients, particularly those displaying violent behavior, are further mistreated by the temple priest, who believes their suffering is linked to spiritual or supernatural causes. This practice reflects deeply ingrained misconceptions, not just about mental illness, but about tribal India's supposed immunity to such challenges. Contrary to the romanticized notion that tribal communities live in harmony and happiness, emerging studies reveal that mental health issues in tribal regions are just as prevalent and concerning as in other parts of the country. The lack of awareness, limited healthcare access, and cultural stigmas surrounding mental health exacerbate the suffering of these individuals. This ground report sheds light on this grim reality, advocating for urgent attention to mental health care and reforms in tribal areas.

Note - The persons shown in this report have given their consent to Main Bhi Bharat team.
